notes: Evals 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 are self-contained: their fixtures live in evals/fixtures/ inside this skill (4 reuses 1; 5 targets partial failure and loops; 6 is the clean false-positive control; 7 distinguishes actual defenses from independent refund and failed-payment recovery defects; 9 tests an unverified re-audit antecedent; 10 tests independent root causes, historical snapshots and impact-based severity). Evals 8 and 9 need setup: copy their previous-orders-module.md to <working-dir>/systemic-out/orders-module.md BEFORE the run. Substitute the absolute skill path for <SKILL_DIR>. Eval 3 is a template requiring a real target supplied at runtime. Reports go under systemic-out/ in the working directory, outside the fixture directories. Isolate runs to prevent stale reports; for re-audits seed the correct previous report. No expected finding count forbids additional evidence-backed defects. Assertions evaluate causal evidence and impact, not agreement with a preferred phrasing. Output selection is tested separately: cases 1-10 explicitly request full to preserve their detailed-format assertions; 11 uses no mode and must default to functional; 12 explicitly requests full on the same invoice fixture; 13 reauds an older full report in default functional mode. Case 13 requires the same previous-report setup as 9. Both modes keep evidence, labels, confidence, impact limits and finding history; only presentation differs.

evals.name: seeded-defects-code
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the orders module at <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/orders/ (README.md, models.py, operations.py, webhook.py). I want to find inconsistencies in its states and operations before it reaches production. Use output full.
evals.expected_output: A report following the skill's exact structure that models the orders system (elements, operators, declared vs built machine) and covers the seeded obligations without imposing a maximum finding count with file:line evidence, honesty labels and calibrated severities, plus a missing-piece synthesis.
assertions: Detects the closure violation: refund() writes status 'refund_pending' which is not in the STATUS set (models.py vs operations.py) — rated critical or high
Detects the illegal representable state: mark_paid() sets paid_at/status without any guard on current status (a draft order can become paid) — rated critical or high
Detects the declared-vs-built contradiction: cancel() has no guard while the README forbids canceling a shipped order — rated critical or high
Detects the ambiguous operator: apply_discount() switches semantics on value<=1 (fraction vs absolute) while the README says percentage 0-100 — rated critical or high (value=1.0 zeroes the total)
Detects the broken symmetry: hold() exists but no release/resume operation exists anywhere in the module — rated high (paused orders have no exit, blocking business flow)
Detects the unreachable state: in_review is declared (README + STATUS) but no operation ever produces it — rated medium (a dead component; no data is trapped)

Detects the idempotency flaw: handle_payment_webhook() has no dedup by event_id although the README warns the provider retries/duplicates — rated critical or high (duplicate Payment records and an inflated total_paid)
Detects the double source of truth: Order.total stored while calc_total() exists, and add_item() does not update total — rated high (the webhook decides paid using the drifting stored total)
Detects the partial-failure risk in ship(): inventory reserved, courier.notify may raise, status not yet written, no transaction/compensation — rated critical or high

Severities are calibrated by demonstrated impact, not uniform or domain labels: unreachable in_review stays medium; a critical rating needs supported severe consequences. No critical finding is mandatory solely because money or persisted data is involved.
Report includes a mermaid state diagram
Every finding carries an honesty label (INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY)
Every finding carries a severity (critical/high/medium/low)
Findings cite file:line (or file+function) evidence
Evidence quotes match the actual content of the cited fixture files (no paraphrase presented as a quote, no references to lines that do not say what the finding claims)

No two findings share a root cause: a defect that surfaces under several checks (e.g. cancel()'s missing guard as both a transition hole and the declared-vs-built contradiction) appears as ONE finding that names the other manifestation, not as two findings
Report includes a missing-piece/root-cause synthesis (e.g. a single guarded transition operator would prevent several findings at once)
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
No artifact is published, no HTML is rendered and no server/localhost preview is started to display the report
Every finding states demonstrated impact, impact not verified and confidence with an evidence basis; confidence and severity are independent.
Uses full output because the current request explicitly selects it; mode selection does not weaken evidence, refutation, severity or source verification.

evals.name: saga-compensations-and-loops
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the booking saga at <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/booking-saga/ (README.md, steps.py, saga.py, worker.py). It runs across three external providers with no shared transaction and I am worried about what happens when a step fails. Use output full.
evals.expected_output: A report that models the saga as a system, maps each step to its compensation, and concentrates on partial failure (check 6) and feedback loops (check 12) — the two checks the other fixtures barely exercise — with file:line evidence, honesty labels and severities.
assertions: Detects the compensation off-by-one: _compensate_from() slices STEPS[:i-1] instead of STEPS[:i], so the step immediately before the failure is never compensated (saga.py, _compensate_from)
Traces the off-by-one to money: when reserve_hotel fails, charge_card is never compensated, so the customer stays charged for a trip that was not booked — contradicting the guarantee and rule 3
Detects that a failure in the FIRST step makes STEPS[:i-1] evaluate to STEPS[:-1], compensating two steps that never ran (releasing a null flight_ref and refunding a null charge_ref)
Detects that the compensation loop has no error handling: a compensation that raises skips every remaining compensation and leaves no record (saga.py, _compensate_from)
Detects that no saga state is ever persisted: booking.completed lives in memory and is never written, so a crash between steps leaves the invariant with no maintainer
Detects that booking.completed is appended to but never read by the compensation logic — a tracked source of truth the recovery path ignores
Detects the retry amplification in handle(): an unbounded while True with no backoff that ALSO re-enqueues the same booking on every failure, so each failure multiplies the work (worker.py, handle)
Detects the alert feedback loop: every failure notifies on-call, and on_alert() re-enqueues the booking, so the alert causes the action that causes the alert (worker.py, handle + on_alert)
Detects the dead-letter loop: drain_dead_letter() re-enqueues everything with no filter and nothing verifies the underlying problem was fixed, contrary to rule 6 (worker.py, drain_dead_letter)
Detects that nothing ever writes to the dead-letter queue although rule 6 declares it: drain_dead_letter() drains a queue no operator fills

Describes timeout-driven retry as conditional on cumulative provider latency exceeding TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2. Does NOT infer frequent or expected timeouts from slow alone; real latency and timeout frequency are not verifiable without measurements or explicit bounds.
Names check 6 (invariants and partial failure) and check 12 (feedback loops) explicitly as the checks that carry the analysis
Report includes a mermaid diagram of the saga and its compensation paths
Every finding carries an honesty label (INCONSISTENCY/RISK/AMBIGUITY) and a severity
Findings cite file:line evidence
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
Uses full output because the current request explicitly selects it; mode selection does not weaken evidence, refutation, severity or source verification.

evals.name: clean-code-no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the ticket module at <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/clean-ticket/ (README.md, models.py, operations.py). Is this lifecycle consistent? Use output full.
evals.expected_output: A report on a deliberately correct module: it must confirm the lifecycle is consistent, say concretely WHY it is, and resist manufacturing findings. This is the only eval whose primary signal is what the skill does NOT report — every other fixture rewards finding things, so this one measures the false-positive rate that determines whether the tool can be trusted.
assertions: PRIMARY: reports ZERO critical and ZERO high findings

States explicitly what is correct rather than only listing problems: apply_transition is the single writer of status, TRANSITIONS is the declared source of truth, and every non-terminal state has an exit
Confirms closure: apply_transition can only write values present in TRANSITIONS, all of which are in STATUS
Confirms idempotency by construction: a repeated operation returns False and changes nothing, because the (status, action) pair is no longer in the table
Does NOT report close() having no inverse as a symmetry violation — closed is a declared terminal state (FINAL_STATUSES, rule 4), and a declared terminal is not a broken duality

Does NOT report the declared limits (no direct reassignment, no spam/duplicate state, no priority or SLA) as defects; they belong in the Limits section, correctly identified as deliberate and documented

Does NOT inflate the two in-memory statements in assign()/resolve() into a partial-failure or atomicity RISK — there is no I/O, no persistence and no multi-system write; a low-severity note is acceptable, a high or critical is a false positive
Does NOT invent concurrency findings: Ticket is an in-memory dataclass with no persistence layer, so check 8 must be reported as not verifiable rather than as a lost update
Does NOT invent states, transitions or operators that are absent from TRANSITIONS and operations.py

MAY legitimately observe that FINAL_STATUSES duplicates a fact derivable from TRANSITIONS (closed is the state with no outgoing transitions) — if reported, it must be rated low, and it is the only finding above informational that the material supports

The check-coverage table gives a verdict for all twelve checks instead of forcing findings: at minimum checks 6, 8 and 12 are marked not verifiable with the reason (in-memory module, no I/O, no queues)
Report still follows the full structure: systems table, mermaid state diagram, limits section
Every finding, if any, carries an honesty label and a severity
Uses full output because the current request explicitly selects it; mode selection does not weaken evidence, refutation, severity or source verification.

evals.name: guarded-elsewhere-refutation
evals.prompt: Run a systemic analysis of the invoices module at <SKILL_DIR>/evals/fixtures/guarded-elsewhere/ (README.md, models.py, guards.py, operations.py, api.py, webhooks.py). Are its lifecycle and operations consistent? Use output full.
evals.expected_output: A report that rejects false absence-of-defense claims using the actual decorator, guarding caller, synchronized total and successful payment replay, while detecting independent refund eligibility, refund replay, failed-payment recovery and retained-item alias risks. Defense presence does not establish correctness on failure. Findings may be separate or grouped only if the distinct causes, traces and repair obligations remain explicit; additional evidence-backed defects are permitted.
assertions: Detects the refund replay defect: the refund route is registered with dedupe_events=False (webhooks.py, with the TODO confession) while rule 4 declares provider retries, so a retried refund event re-runs handle_refund_event and appends a duplicate row to the REFUNDS ledger, violating rule 5's exactly-once — check 7, rated critical or high

Detects that handle_refund_event also bypasses the module's guard discipline: it writes status directly with no @requires_status and no caller-side check, so a refund event can 'reopen' an invoice in any status, not just paid

Detects failed-payment recovery: dedupe adds the event id before the handler succeeds; payment delivered while draft raises InvalidStatus, then issue followed by retry of that same event returns duplicate and leaves issued/unpaid. States this ordering condition and does not call it absence of middleware.

Keeps refund eligibility and replay as independent repair obligations: a paid-state guard still permits P1 -> R1 -> new P2 -> replay R1, while dedupe alone still permits a first refund on void. A common architectural recommendation does not prove one root cause.

Recognizes the concrete alias risk if demonstrated: caller keeps the LineItem passed to add_line, issues the invoice, then changes the retained item quantity; stored total and sum(items) diverge. State the caller-mutation condition, distinguish it from missing _recalc, and avoid assuming every caller does this.
Does NOT report issue()/mark_overdue()/void()/add_line()/remove_line() as missing status guards: the @requires_status decorator in guards.py enforces the precondition before each body runs

Does NOT claim the payment route has no deduplication or that replay of a completed successful payment reapplies it: the default wrapper suppresses that replay. This does NOT exclude evidence-backed failure-recovery findings.

Does NOT claim add_line/remove_line omit _recalc: both synchronize total on their guarded paths. This does NOT prohibit a conditional drift finding through a retained mutable LineItem alias; inspect ownership and actual accessible mutation paths rather than claiming no drift is possible.

Does NOT rate _apply_payment()'s missing internal guard above low: record_payment in api.py is its only caller and enforces rule 2 before calling; a low note about the fragility of a caller-side guard is acceptable
Does NOT report void() having no inverse: void is a declared terminal state, and a declared terminal is not a broken duality
The rejected-candidates table names the refuted traps with the evidence that killed each one (the decorator, the middleware default, the synchronized _recalc, the guarding caller)
Every reported finding carries an honesty label, a severity and file:line evidence
The report is written to a local Markdown file under systemic-out/ and the chat reply states its path
Uses full output because the current request explicitly selects it; mode selection does not weaken evidence, refutation, severity or source verification.
